title: Scale the bar spacer with the spacing scale and text size
head: d844628a0e29
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Fractional spacer sizes lose precision before they are scaled
leads.consequence: A valid layout entry {"id":"omarchy.spacer","size":1.4} at [spacing] scale = 2 yields authoredSize = 1 and span = 2, although scaling the authored 1.4 and rounding once yields 3. This affects the gap in either bar orientation. The previous integer span also truncated 1.4 at scale 1, but the new contract of scaling the authored value is not met at other scales. Use a real for authoredSize until the final Math.round, and add a fractional-input assertion. Source-derived, not run in QML.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus optional note c (int truncation of fractional sizes); published as a collapsed optional note, pre-existing behaviour.

leads.summary: Zero-size rationale for avoiding Style.space() is contradicted by Style.space() itself, and the test cannot distinguish them
leads.consequence: The code comment says Style.space() would turn size 0 into one pixel, but Style.space(0) returns 0: spaceReal(0) returns 0 and space() exits at n <= 0 before its positive-size minimum. Replacing Math.round(Style.spaceReal(authoredSize)) with Style.space(authoredSize) would satisfy every new test assertion, including size 0. The real difference is at small positive sizes under small scales: size 1 at spacing.scale 0.25 becomes span 0 and hidden with the PR, but Style.space(1) yields span 1 and visible. Clarify why that small-size disappearance is intended, and assert this case if preserving it matters. Source-derived, no Quickshell run.
leads.triage: corroborated; Same as Opus finding 2, reproduced; published in the collapsed More findings block.

leads.summary: New test cannot catch an unscaled default-sized spacer
leads.consequence: The assertion for the unset size checks defaultSpacer only at the initial base-size 12. A plausible regression, for example `span: settings && settings.size !== undefined ? Math.round(Style.spaceReal(authoredSize)) : 12`, passes every assertion in this test yet leaves an unset spacer at 12 when base-size is 20 (expected 20). Add assertions on defaultSpacer after font-size and spacing changes, and on verticalSpacer.span after reflow. Source-derived mutant, not executed.
leads.triage: verified_dropped; Coordinator confirmed with rg -n that defaultSpacer is asserted only at base-size 12 (test lines 72, 78). Coverage gap only; no demonstrated surviving mutant, so omitted per the optional-test rule.

limits: No compositor or desktop allocated. No Quickshell or repository tests were executed. H1 uses Qt declarative upstream 6.9 as source evidence; Omarchy's unversioned quickshell package list does not pin a Qt version. No merged open-PR tests were run.

flags.claim: At default settings the span matches the base for every probed size; the only exceptions are negative sizes and sizes above 2^31-1, which are hidden in both.
flags.why: Overgeneralised from a single probed value. Among the probed sizes above 2^31-1, size 1e10 did not differ: it gave span 1410065408, visible, in both base and head. Only 2147483648 differed (base -2147483648, head 0, hidden in both). Among negative sizes, -0.4 matched (0 in both); only -3 differed (base -3, head 0, hidden in both). My final.md line 51 has the same overgeneralisation ('a size above 2^31-1 (both hidden)'), which is an inconsistency with my own edge table.
flags.disposition: fixed; Verified bullet now names the only differing probed sizes (-3 and 2147483648), both hidden in both versions.

flags.claim: Outcome: The new test fails for testers whose own `shell.toml` sets a non-default text size.
flags.why: It is a race, not an unconditional failure: 41 of 46 runs failed with base-size 16 in HOME, and 5 passed. Only base-size 16 was run; that any other non-12 base-size also trips an assertion is derived from source (the unset-size check expects 12 and gets base-size), not run. The Outcome also drops the other half of my suggested outcome, that the scaling itself works and the default size is unchanged, so a reader of the visible text alone may take the feature to be broken.
flags.disposition: fixed; Outcome: 'usually fails (41 of 46 runs)'. Did not add the positive clause, because the Outcome must not open with what passed; Verified covers it.

flags.claim: ... into `Style`, usually before the `Qt.callLater` callback runs.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. The ordering was measured only in the offscreen sandbox (timing probe: 16 at callLater in 18 of 20 runs). My report states that startup timing on a real Wayland session may differ. The Test scope line mentions offscreen runs, so this is minor.
flags.disposition: fixed; 'in offscreen sandbox runs usually before the Qt.callLater callback'.

flags.claim: `readonly property real authoredSize` would scale fractional sizes exactly.
flags.why: Dropped qualifier. My report said 'and `span` stays an int': the span is still rounded to a whole pixel, so 'exactly' is too strong. The `real` variant was not run; the value 11 comes from spaceReal(6.6) at base-size 20 in the probe.
flags.disposition: fixed; 'would scale the fraction before rounding (6.6 would give 11 at base-size 20)'.

## Automated AI review > **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Outcome:** The new test usually fails (41 of 46 runs) when the tester's own `shell.toml` sets a non-default text size. ### The new test reads the tester's own `shell.toml` `quickshell` inherits `HOME`, so `Color.qml` loads `~/.config/omarchy/shell.toml` (written by `omarchy display text size`) and the theme's `shell.toml` into `Style`, in offscreen sandbox runs usually before the `Qt.callLater` callback. With `[font] base-size = 16` there, the test failed 41 of 46 runs with `size 6 at base-size 12 should be 6, got 8`. **Impact:** false or intermittent `./test/shell` failures for anyone who changed their text size; no product impact. **Suggested change:** Run the fixture's `quickshell` with its own `HOME` and `XDG_*` directories under `$test_tmp`, as `indicator-contract-test.sh` does.
Reproducer (fails at d844628) # Reproducer: bar-spacer-scale-test.sh reads the developer's own shell.toml Reviewed head: d844628a0e299b9bcfbe504f4607c50a1a45458a (omacom/omarchy PR #13593). The test runs `quickshell` with the caller's `HOME`. `Color.qml` then loads `~/.config/omarchy/shell.toml` (the file `omarchy display text size` writes) and the current theme's `shell.toml`, and pushes them into `Style.applyShellValues()`. The load usually lands before the test's `Qt.callLater` callback, so the first two assertions, which assume `base-size = 12` and `[spacing] scale = 1` (size 6 gives 6, an unset size gives 12), see the developer's values instead. ## Steps From a checkout of the PR head, in a session where `./test/shell` runs (the test calls `require_compositor`): ```bash tmp_home=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$tmp_home/.config/omarchy" # The same content `omarchy display text size 16` writes. printf '[font]\nbase-size = 16\n' >"$tmp_home/.config/omarchy/shell.toml" HOME="$tmp_home" bash test/shell.d/bar-spacer-scale-test.sh echo "exit=$?" rm -rf "$tmp_home" ``` ## Actual output Captured in an isolated sandbox with Quickshell 0.3.1 and `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`. There was no compositor, so `require_compositor` was replaced with `return 0` in a disposable copy of `base-test.sh`; nothing else in the test changed. Output of one failing run (stderr, then the exit status): ``` [three INFO lines omitted: sandbox paths, shell ID and log location] WARN: $HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE is unset. Cannot connect to hyprland. INFO: Configuration Loaded DEBUG qml: RESULT fail size 6 at base-size 12 should be 6, got 8 not ok - bar spacer size follows the spacing scale and text size exit=1 ``` Repeat counts with that `shell.toml` in `HOME`: 41 of 46 runs failed with exactly this message (batches of 5/5, 18/20, 18/20 and 0/1), and 5 passed. That makes it a race between the file load and the callback that the load usually wins, not a deterministic failure. A separate probe logged `Style.fontBaseSize` at the `Qt.callLater` point: it was already 16 in 18 of 20 runs, and in a single run with an empty `HOME` it was 12. A theme `shell.toml` with `[spacing] scale = 1.25` under `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/` failed 2 of 3 runs with the same message. Control: the existing `test/shell.d/bar-icon-geometry-test.sh`, which compares against live `Style` tokens instead of fixed numbers, passed under the same `HOME` (`ok - bar icons share slot and baseline geometry`). ## Fix check Giving the fixture's `quickshell` its own `HOME`, as `test/shell.d/indicator-contract-test.sh` and `bar-widget-contract-test.sh` already do, makes the result independent of the caller's config: ```diff output=$(timeout 15 env \ + HOME="$test_tmp/home" \ + XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$test_tmp/home/.config" \ + XDG_CACHE_HOME="$test_tmp/home/.cache" \ + XDG_STATE_HOME="$test_tmp/home/.local/state" \ QML2_IMPORT_PATH="$ROOT/shell${QML2_IMPORT_PATH:+:$QML2_IMPORT_PATH}" \ ``` With that change and the same `base-size = 16` file in the caller's `HOME`, 20 of 20 runs printed `ok - bar spacer size follows the spacing scale and text size`. Against the merge-base `Spacer.qml` it still fails as intended: ``` DEBUG qml: RESULT fail size 6 at base-size 15 should be 8, got 6 not ok - bar spacer size follows the spacing scale and text size ``` Resetting the values at the start of the callback also works: ```diff Component.onCompleted: Qt.callLater(function() { + shellValues({}) if (spacer.span !== 6) return fail("size 6 at base-size 12 should be 6, got " + spacer.span) ``` With the same file in `HOME`, this variant passed 20 of 20 runs, while the unmodified test failed 18 of the 20 runs interleaved with them. Against the merge-base `Spacer.qml` the variant still fails with `RESULT fail size 6 at base-size 15 should be 8, got 6`.
More findings: the comment's reason for avoiding Style.space() does not hold **The comment's reason for avoiding `Style.space()` does not hold.** `Style.space(0)` returns 0: its 1 px floor applies only to positive values (`Style.qml` lines 214-224), and with `span: Style.space(authoredSize)` the PR's test passes, including `size: 0`. The two formulas differ only when a positive size scales below 0.5 px (for example `size: 1` at `[spacing] scale = 0.4`), where this PR hides the spacer and `space()` keeps 1 px. **Suggested change:** Use `Style.space(authoredSize)` and drop the comment, or reword it if hiding sub-half-pixel spacers is intended.
Reproducer # Reproducer: `Style.space(0)` is 0, so the reason given for not using it does not hold Reviewed head: d844628a0e299b9bcfbe504f4607c50a1a45458a (omacom/omarchy PR #13593). The comment above `span` in `shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Spacer.qml` (lines 11-13) says `Style.space()` "floors a positive value at 1 and would turn `size: 0` into one pixel". In `shell/Commons/Style.qml`, `spaceReal()` returns 0 for any `n <= 0` (lines 214-218), and `space()` returns 0 when `spaceReal()` is `<= 0` (lines 220-224). The 1px floor only applies to positive values, so `Style.space(0)` is 0 and a `size: 0` spacer stays hidden either way. ## Steps From a checkout of the PR head, change the span line to use `Style.space()` and run the PR's own test (it needs a compositor, like the rest of `./test/shell`): ```diff - readonly property int span: Math.round(Style.spaceReal(authoredSize)) + readonly property int span: Style.space(authoredSize) ``` ```bash bash test/shell.d/bar-spacer-scale-test.sh echo "exit=$?" ``` ## Actual output Captured in an isolated sandbox with Quickshell 0.3.1 and `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`. There was no compositor, so `require_compositor` was replaced with `return 0` in a disposable copy of `base-test.sh`. The test file itself was unchanged. It includes the `size: 0` case (`hiddenSpacer.span !== 0 || hiddenSpacer.visible`): ``` ok - bar spacer size follows the spacing scale and text size exit=0 ``` A probe that evaluated `Style.space(0)` and `Style.spaceReal(0)` in the same runtime printed: ``` DEBUG qml: SPACE0 0 SPACEREAL0 0 ``` ## Where the two formulas actually differ Checked with a probe over 33 authored values under 9 shell settings: `Math.round(Style.spaceReal(authoredSize))` and `Style.space(authoredSize)` agree except when a positive size scales to less than 0.5 px. There `space()` keeps 1px and the PR's formula hides the spacer, for example `size: 1` with `[spacing] scale = 0.4` (head span 0 and hidden, `space()` gives 1), or `size: 1` and `size: 2` at `[font] base-size = 1`. The probe's only other mismatches were sizes near the int limit, where the probe compared an int property with an unconverted JavaScript number; stored in the same `int` property, both formulas give the same result there.
Details **Verified** (offscreen sandbox runs at d844628): - `size: 6` gives 5, 6, 8 and 10 at `[font] base-size` 9, 12, 15 and 20, gives 3 at `[spacing] scale = 0.5`, and stays 6 at base-size 20 with `[spacing] scale-with-font = false`. - At default settings the span matches the base for every probed size except `size: -3` (base -3, head 0) and `size: 2147483648` (wraps to a negative int at base, 0 at head); both are hidden in both versions. - A running spacer updates when shell values change or when its `settings` are replaced, matching a freshly created one. - Horizontal bars lay the span along the bar and vertical bars stack it, with the bar size across. - The new test fails on the base with `RESULT fail size 6 at base-size 15 should be 8, got 6`. **Optional notes:** - The comment above the `spacing.scale-with-font` case (test line 94) says "a bar that does not scale with text", but `[bar] scale-with-font = false` does not stop the spacer scaling (size 6 at base-size 20 still gives 10), so the wording can mislead. - `authoredSize` is an `int`, so `size: 6.6` truncates to 6 before scaling (10 at base-size 20, where 6.6 scaled gives 11). The base also truncated; `readonly property real authoredSize` would scale the fraction before rounding (6.6 would give 11 at base-size 20).
--- ## Review information **Test scope:** Source review and offscreen sandbox runs of the PR's test and a size/settings probe (Quickshell 0.3.1) at `d844628`; not checked in a running bar. **AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check. **Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
